name: Sailfish OS
summary: European mobile operating system developed by Jolla, combining a free Linux foundation, the Silica gesture interface and Android AppSupport application compatibility.
license: Hybrid (open-source Mer/GPL foundation and Silica/AppSupport interface under proprietary Jolla licence)

content.introduction: Sailfish OS is a mobile operating system developed by the Finnish company Jolla Ltd., founded in 2011 by former Nokia executives and engineers from the MeeGo project following the abandonment of the Nokia N9.
content.what_is_it: Sailfish OS offers a European alternative to the dominant mobile operating systems. It combines an open-source core based on Linux (Mer Core) with a proprietary user interface entirely driven by touch gestures and an optional compatibility layer for running Android applications.
content.jolla_governance_and_meego_heritage: Direct heir of MeeGo and of the Mer mobile stack, Sailfish OS first equipped the devices designed by Jolla (the Jolla Phone in 2013 and the Jolla Tablet in 2015). After a phase of diversification towards institutional integrators and partner manufacturers, Jolla reaffirmed its mainstream and community positioning with the release of the Jolla C2 Community Phone smartphone and of the major version Sailfish OS 5.0 (Tampella).
content.silica_interface_and_gestural_paradigm: The graphical interface of Sailfish OS, called Silica, is designed in C++ and Qt Quick / QML above the Lipstick Wayland compositor. Silica adopts a fluid gesture ergonomic philosophy allowing full one-handed use without hardware or software navigation buttons. The home screen presents the active applications as dynamic cards ("covers") displaying live information and quick action buttons. A horizontal swipe from the outside of the screen instantly switches to the home screen or the events panel. Access to the options is obtained through the "pulley menu", a continuous vertical slide from the top of the screen revealing the commands without hiding the main application content.
content.hybrid_architecture_and_appsupport: The architecture of Sailfish OS is split into two distinct strata: an open-source foundation (Sailfish Core / Mer) and a proprietary layer developed by Jolla. The free foundation includes the standard Linux kernel, the glibc library, systemd, Wayland, the ConnMan network stack and RPM package management through the Zypper tool. On compatible devices and under the commercial Sailfish X licence, the system includes AppSupport (formerly Alien Dalvik). AppSupport runs a complete Android runtime in an isolated LXC container, sharing 3D hardware acceleration, sound and notifications with the host system, thus making it possible to run ordinary Android applications alongside native Qt/C++ applications without slow software emulation.
content.hardware_programs_and_ecosystem_limits: The deployment model of Sailfish OS rests on terminals produced directly by Jolla (such as the original Jolla Phone or the Jolla C2) and on the official Sailfish X porting programme, targeting mainly Sony Xperia smartphones (Xperia 10 II, III, IV and V ranges) through Sony's Open Devices Program. A free trial version gives access to the base operating system, while a paid commercial licence unlocks AppSupport, XT9 predictive input and Exchange ActiveSync synchronisation. Despite its technical maturity, Sailfish OS remains constrained by the small size of its native application ecosystem and the absence of Google Play Integrity certification, limiting the use of certain banking applications or of services protected by Widevine L1 DRM.
content.release_model_and_stop_releases: Sailfish OS releases are organised by major versions, each series carrying a Finnish theme (Tampere region, UNESCO world heritage, national parks, rivers, lakes). The official version table lists for the 5 series the releases 5.0.0.5 to 5.0.0.71, the most recent dated 30 October 2025. Some entries are marked "stop release": 5.0.0.71 (30 October 2025) is associated with the Jolla C2 and Mind2, with AppSupport 13, with microG 0.3.6 and with the esr91 browser engine; 4.6.0.15 (20 September 2024) adds an /opt2 partition for the XA2 and Xperia 10 and is flagged as the last version for the Jolla C, Tablet, Xperia X and Gemini PDA. In the cases listed above, these markers accompany structural changes of partition, application stack or supported hardware.
content.deploiement_et_mises_a_jour: Deployment relies on the official documentation, which distinguishes the flashing of a device, the installation of Sailfish OS, its reinstallation, the update of the system and the update of the vendor image. A recovery mode is documented separately, as are the procedures for locking the device and setting the security code. Updates are published as successive versions, with release notes and a known issues page maintained by the project; the versions called "stop releases" serve as a mandatory stage before moving to the next branch.
content.securite_systeme_et_confinement: Security relies on mechanisms documented at system level: user data are encrypted, applications are confined by Firejail, connectivity goes through a firewall with native VPN support, and system services are confined by means of systemd. The project also announces MDM-type fleet management capability at operating system level, as well as automatic backups. The user documentation covers in detail data encryption, device locking and the firewall.
content.rpm_packaging_and_device_variants: Native software is packaged as RPM, and the device side uses PackageKit with a libzypp backend to manage the RPM database; binary diffing and delta-rpm upgrades are supported to reduce the bandwidth needed for an update. What distinguishes the model is the device variant: each variant is defined by a pattern file that describes the initial filesystem content and the packages to install, and can differ by region, operator or hardware platform, with segregation enforced both when an image is created and when a device is updated. Updates therefore do not flow from a single public archive to every handset; they are controlled per variant through the SSU and Store services, and vendor-specific content such as licenses and artwork can be preinstalled either as packages or on a dedicated partition. Android applications use the APK format separately, handled by the apkd service that mediates their installation, removal and upgrade.
content.advantages: Sailfish OS offers highly fluid gesture navigation without on-screen button clutter, performant visual multitasking with interactive cards, a modern Linux foundation based on RPM and Wayland, and a well-integrated Android compatibility layer limiting dependence on proprietary ecosystems.
content.disadvantages: The Silica interface and the AppSupport technology remain closed and proprietary, the complete Sailfish X licence for Sony devices is paid, and compatibility with Android applications requiring certified Google Play services is not guaranteed.
content.who_is_it_for: Sailfish OS is intended for smartphone users looking for an alternative touch user experience of European origin and careful design, while retaining the ability to run ordinary Android applications on officially validated hardware (Sony Xperia or Jolla C2).
content.who_is_it_not_for: Sailfish OS is not suited to users requiring a 100% free and end-to-end auditable system (such as Mobian or Nura), nor to owners of smartphones not officially supported by Jolla who do not wish to resort to community ports.
content.verdict: Carried by the legacy of Nokia and MeeGo, Sailfish OS has maintained itself for more than a decade as an independent mobile system, combining a Qt gesture interface and an Android interoperability bridge within a hybrid software framework.

relations.name: Ubuntu Touch
relations.note: Free mobile operating system maintained by UBports offering a convergent interface competing with Sailfish OS.

relations.name: Nura
relations.note: Mobile Linux distribution based on Alpine Linux oriented towards hardware longevity and free components.

relations.name: Mobian
relations.note: Debian-based mobile distribution using the Phosh shell and the upstream mainline Linux kernel.

relations.name: LineageOS
relations.note: Free mobile operating system based on AOSP, constituting the reference for alternative phone ROMs.
